title: An HDR copy's fallback keeps the picture's range
description: JS-088 and JS-133 make a copy whose keyframe index is found wrong go on as an encode of the copy's codec. The fallback's picture is always `format=yuv420p`, 8 bits with no colour tags, and a copy has no tone mapping (`Spec.ToneMap` is empty), so an HDR10 or HLG HEVC or AV1 copy, which is copied only to a client whose profile shows the range (master playlist `VIDEO-RANGE=PQ` or `HLG`), would go on mid-film as PQ or HLG samples squeezed into 8 bits and tagged as SDR: washed out or banded, the failure JS-088 exists to hide. Not observed yet (found reading internal/transcode/ffmpeg.go after JS-133). PRODUCT.md: no film is second-class, and an HDR viewer keeps HDR.
acceptanceCriteria: Recorded in compat/captures beside av1-fallback-12.4.md, with the commands that reproduce it, for an HDR10 HEVC copy and an HDR10 AV1 copy: what ffprobe says of the copy and of today's fallback of it, for the init segment and for the frames of each (pixel format and bit depth, primaries, transfer, matrix, range, mastering display and content light level), and whether today's fallback is tone mapped

Recorded there with the script that reproduces it, in jellyfin-web 12.4's hls.js 1.6.16 in Chromium: a 10-bit PQ copy's playlist whose later segments are today's fallback, and again with a 10-bit fallback carrying the copy's tags, each segment led by its own init, played forward across the change, then seeked back into a copy segment (a 10-bit init after an 8-bit one) and forward across it again; for each direction the frames shown, video.error, whether a dialog shows, whether currentTime keeps its place, and whether the colours Chrome draws of the same picture differ before and after the change; for AV1 always, and for HEVC where the observing browser plays it, otherwise marked not observed

The record names the format the fallback of an HDR copy takes, and the checks below hold the build to it: 10 bits with the copy's tags and no tone mapping, unless the player was seen to refuse that (video.error, a dialog or no frames in either direction), which goes to the owner and is not settled by the build sending another format

With a real worker and ffmpeg, on Ubuntu 24.04's ffmpeg 6.1 and on ffmpeg 9, the fallback of each of an HDR10 HEVC, HLG HEVC, HDR10 AV1 and HLG AV1 copy, and of an HDR10+ HEVC copy as its HDR10 picture, is 10 bits in the profile the master playlist's CODECS names (HEVC Main 10, AV1 profile 0 at 10 bits), and ffprobe shows the copy's own primaries, transfer, matrix and range for the fallback's init segment alone and for the frames of every fallback segment as it is answered (its init in front)

That fallback is the copy's own picture: its decoded frames are nearer the source's frames at the same times (scaled alike, at 10 bits) than the frames of the tone-mapped fallback today's build makes of the same film, and its ffmpeg command has no tone-mapping filter and no 8-bit pixel format on the way

The fallback of an SDR copy (8 or 10 bit; H.264, HEVC or AV1) and of an H.264 copy in any range has the ffmpeg arguments and the 8-bit picture it has today, and every JS-088 and JS-133 check passes as written, bar those that pin OutputVersion's number and the hashes that follow from it

A fallback run of an HDR10 HEVC copy and of an HDR10 AV1 copy begun at segment 1, at a middle segment and at the last, as a restart begins, splices with the earlier segments of a run from the start: a byte-identical init segment (so the same bit depth and tags), the same number of frames, frame times within 1 ms, audio packet times within 0.5 ms and no decoder warning across the join that the run from the start lacks, on Ubuntu 24.04's ffmpeg 6.1 and on ffmpeg 9

When the worker process making an HDR copy's fallback is killed mid-job, another worker process makes the rest from the first missing segment, the waiting request is answered with no error status, and the two workers' segments join as in the criterion before (invariant 22), for HEVC and for AV1; it holds three runs in a row on two CPUs under ffmpeg 6.1 (test/ffmpeg61.sh, JELLYSCALE_TEST_CPUS=0-1, -count=3)

The price (Spec.Cost) of an HDR copy's fallback is at least the CPU time (user plus system) its own ffmpeg command uses per second of film, measured through a worker for a 1080p and a 4K 24 fps HDR10 source, for HEVC and for AV1, on ffmpeg 6.1 and on ffmpeg 9; docs/transcoding.md records the machine, the ffmpeg and encoder versions, the CPU and wall-clock figures (wall-clock no slower than the film plays) and the cost table's rows, and the 4K copy's fallback is 1920x1080 as before

A worker of the release before (output version 6) never claims the fallback job of an HDR copy: OutputVersion is raised (invariant 59), so no 8-bit or tone-mapped segment is stored under the new fallback's hash

In the e2e tier, jellyfin-web in Chromium plays an HDR10 film with keyframes 5 to 7 s apart as a copy (VideoCodec=copy, master VIDEO-RANGE=PQ; the HEVC film when E2E_HEVC=1, the AV1 one otherwise, as in CI), the job finds its index wrong while the viewer is more than 4 s before the bad point on stored copy segments, and the viewer reaches 30 s past it with no Playback Error dialog, no /Videos/ request answered 400 or more, no playlist or segment request abandoned, no video.error, no corrupted frames, at least 480 of those 30 s' 720 frames shown, and currentTime never going back by more than 4 s or forward by more than 1 s

In that scenario the index is then recorded dropped, a worker's ffmpeg encoded the picture with the copy's codec, and a fallback segment as the browser was answered it is 10 bits with the copy's transfer (PQ), so the scenario fails on today's 8-bit fallback

A Dolby Vision copy whose base layer is HDR10 (profiles 8.1 and 7 in HEVC, 10.1 in AV1) or HLG (8.4) falls back at 10 bits with its base layer's primaries, transfer, matrix and range, as in the fourth criterion, and one whose base layer is SDR (8.2) as an SDR copy does; or, for each kind left out, docs/transcoding.md names it, says why and says what the viewer gets instead, and a check holds the build to what the docs say

docs/transcoding.md says what an HDR copy's fallback keeps (10 bits, primaries, transfer, matrix, range) and what the record shows it does not (HDR10 mastering display and content light level, HDR10+ and Dolby Vision dynamic metadata, lines above 1080), each loss written as a gap
notes: The JS-133 architecture review noted the 10-bit AV1 fallback is 8-bit, observed to play; this task asks what it looks like, and covers HEVC (JS-088) too. Observe before building.
